<description>
Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36755

To cover `-rpcservertimeout` behavior our test expected the Bitcoin Core HTTP server to disconnect the test framework client after the configured duration but also *before* a somewhat arbitrary upper bound. This was helpful during development of #35182 but has led to false negatives in CI on platforms that are just plain slow.

Solve the flakiness by simply deleting the test case. Note that a regression is still caught by both the functional test and unit test suite. #36159 added a mock clock in the unit test to assert the disconnect timing. A server with no timeout would also fail the functional test which will time out during `sock.recv()` waiting for the EOF.

Both regression test failures can be observed on top of this branch by disabling rpcservertimeout:

```diff
diff --git a/src/httpserver.cpp b/src/httpserver.cpp
index 069eace507..7a090c4ca8 100644
--- a/src/httpserver.cpp
+++ b/src/httpserver.cpp
@@ -1205,7 +1205,7 @@ bool HTTPRemoteClient::ShouldDisconnect(MockableSteadyClock::time_point now, std
                  "HTTP client idle timeout %s (id=%llu)",
                  m_origin,
                  m_id);
-        return true;
+        return false;
     // Disconnect this client because the server is shutting down and we need to
     // disconnect all clients... Unless the client is still being handled by a
     // worker thread, in which case we'd rather continue the I/O loop (but might

```
</description>

<commits>
75a23e7d36 test: drop flaky "server too slow" check from interface_http.py
</commits>

<files>
test/functional/interface_http.py  +6/-6

(test/bench/ci lines: 12)
</files>

<patch>
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_http.py b/test/functional/interface_http.py
index 28d1c04f36..acbf176cac 100755
--- a/test/functional/interface_http.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_http.py
@@ -93,14 +93,14 @@ class BitcoinHTTPConnection:
         # Wait for response, but expect a timeout disconnection
         start = time.monotonic()
         response1 = self.recv_raw()
-        stop = time.monotonic()
+        duration = time.monotonic() - start
         # Server disconnected with EOF
         assert_equal(response1, b"")
-        # Server disconnected within an acceptable range of time:
-        # not immediately, and not too far over the configured duration.
-        # This allows for some jitter in the test between client and server.
-        duration = stop - start
-        assert duration <= seconds + 2, f"Server disconnected too slow: {duration} > {seconds}"
+        # Server did not disconnect before the configured idle duration
+        # (allowing 1s of jitter between client and server). There is no
+        # upper bound: slow CI machines can overshoot arbitrarily, and the
+        # socket timeout (rpc_timeout) already catches a server that never
+        # disconnects. Exact timing is covered by httpserver_tests.
         assert duration >= seconds - 1, f"Server disconnected too fast: {duration} < {seconds}"
         # The connection is definitely closed.
         assert self.sock_closed()

</patch>
(Diff from merge base to head, smallest files first.)
